_about: Commit-replay raw data for dev-cockpit (marein/dev-cockpit), used by docs/claims.md #19 and docs/evaluations/evaluation-commit-replay-results.md. This file is the summary form: the 1.3 GB of per-commit JSON it was derived from is NOT in git and has never been tracked (`.data/` is gitignored).

criterion_versions._note: A finding count is meaningless without the commit of metricgate that produced it AND the policy file it was given. The original report used a pair that is neither of the two below; iter-30 proved that a 29-line policy difference (186-line policy.yaml at 59e0a24^ instead of the 157-line version at d5cb01c) inflated every metric count and added 5 rule families the archive has at zero.

archive_original_report.metricgate_commit: unknown / not recoverable (between c701576 and d5cb01c)
archive_original_report.verification: mg-era-bin check . -config /tmp/policy-era.yaml at 396cd3cd8f -> total 2174 / files 555 / errors 222, equal to devcockpit/396cd3cd8f.json line for line

iter30_old.note: test-no-assert results are DIRECTLY comparable to the archive's (identical 1783/215); the other rule families are NOT, because of the policy version

iter30_new.metricgate_commit: 739aa11 (main at the time of the replay)

test_no_assert_iter31.criterion: Benchmark* removed from scope (prefix gate is Test* only, signature gate is *testing.T only)

rule_family_totals._note: Summed over the 289 archived per-commit JSON files. These five rows are exactly reproducible from the archive: fan-out, cyclomatic-complexity, npath-complexity, cognitive-complexity, function-length. The other rows are archive-derived but the report's table disagrees with them for 13 of 18 rows (see unreproducible_rows below).
rule_family_totals.unit: findings instances (one per (commit, file, line, rule))

unreproducible_rows._note: docs/evaluations/evaluation-commit-replay-results.md section 2 prints a 'rule-family total' table. 5 of its 18 rows equal the archive findings total; the other 13 match neither findings, nor commit counts, nor distinct files, nor distinct anchors, nor metric-snapshot threshold counts. Every aggregation tried is listed in evaluation-iter30-tna-recalibration.md section 5. Treat those 13 rows as an unknown aggregation, NOT as a different measurement.

four_zero_rows_are_explained_by_the_poli.boolean-params: warn: 2, error: off -- warnings land in metric snapshots only, never as findings
four_zero_rows_are_explained_by_the_poli.todo-comment: enabled: false (both the go and java sections)
four_zero_rows_are_explained_by_the_poli.empty-block: configured only in the java section, severity: warning with no threshold that fires

test_no_assert_recalibration._note: This is the table docs/claims.md #19 and the results report's 215/289 sentence now rest on. findings = instances; commits = commits with at least one; anchors = distinct (file, line); the archive column and iter30_old agree exactly, which is what establishes the archive as trustworthy.

the_215_mechanism.reading: 215/289 is one function counted once per commit in 215 consecutive commits, not 215 independent events. It was introduced at index 75 and present in every commit afterwards.
the_215_mechanism.source_note: the test asserts by not returning: 'If Publish blocked on a full subscriber this would deadlock and the test would time out.'

corpus_suite._note: the 5-package corpus, 110 _test.go files, is a different corpus from dev-cockpit; these numbers are the criterion comparison on it
corpus_suite.row: go-humanize v1.0.1, google/uuid v1.6.0, google/pprof, mattn/go-isatty, modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk v1.8.0

reproduce.recompute_rule_family_totals: python3 -c "import json,glob,collections; c=collections.Counter(); [c.update([x['ruleId']]) for f in glob.glob('.data/commit-replay/devcockpit/*.json') for x in json.load(open(f))['findings']]; print(c.most_common())"
reproduce.replay_one_commit_era_correct: git worktree add /tmp/mg-era d5cb01c && go -C /tmp/mg-era build -o /tmp/mg-era-bin ./cmd/metricgate && git show d5cb01c:policy.yaml > /tmp/policy-era.yaml && (cd /tmp/dev-cockpit && git checkout -q 396cd3cd8f && /tmp/mg-era-bin check . -config /tmp/policy-era.yaml -format json | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['files'], len(d['findings']), sum(1 for f in d['findings'] if f['severity']=='error'))")
reproduce.replay_289_both_criteria: cli? no: use /tmp/replay30/run.sh shape -- one clone per binary, sequential checkouts, per-commit JSON. Parallel shards on one clone fail with checkout_failed (index.lock).
reproduce.note: the 1.3 GB of raw per-commit JSON is not in this repository. If it is gone, only the totals in this file survive, and the 13 unreproducible rows become unfixable.

history.why_this_file_exists: iter-30 found that the claim this data supports was being read off a machine-local directory. The data still existed, so the claim was re-derived rather than re-flagged as an upper bound; this summary keeps the derivation reproducible without committing 1.3 GB.
